answer: A refundable stake bond resists Sybils: each agent identity must lock a deposit before earning or voting, and peers can slash it if the identity is proved duplicated or its work faked. Like a ridge narrowing many paths into one guarded pass, the bond forces an attacker to pay separately for every fake identity instead of copying one for free. Honest newcomers still join easily, since good behavior returns the deposit, while the velvet ease of signup hides no cost: a thousand Sybils need a thousand deposits, and yarrow weeds of fake accounts wither when their bonds are forfeited.
